c5d51aa7c50818c5981fb74368a3a8e63e18cf15.summary: Forcepoint Security Labs reports that the Carbanak financially motivated criminal group used a trojanized RTF document with encoded VBScript. A new ggldr module uses Google Apps Script, Google Sheets and Google Forms for command-and-control, creating a unique spreadsheet per victim. Forcepoint says it notified Google and that its TRITON ACE customers are protected.

c589d0b60dbcddcd02590499a58f0d37c6d6c3a1.summary: Summit Route blog post on a malicious public AWS AMI (community image). The author started the AMI in an isolated VPC, snapshotted its root volume and mounted it for analysis. Found a cron file tied to a miner-and-worm campaign that appears to use GitHub-hosted repos and free top-level domains. The report links it to the AWS CLI CVE-2018-15869 and to the Xbash malware, as described in a Palo Alto Networks write-up. The author also built a CloudMapper command to check existing EC2 instances against public AMIs.

hedges: The author believes it is not possible to analyze an AMI without starting it as an EC2 instance.
The author believes the 2018-04-17 cron entries show the original download server, and that the instance was first exploited then.
The author says the change in cron download targets is likely just the adversary changing how their malware works.
One possibility is that the creator of the AMI had been a victim and was infected before creating it.
The GitHub repository appears to be the central repo used by this actor.
The author says the AMI provider did not know much about its origin.
The author notes there is no way they know of to easily confirm the Ubuntu account ID.
AWS said there were no infected Community AMIs to its knowledge, and the author says AWS appears to have taken action.

c59a9712231310a14b27efe4a03041ca31f67049.summary: Sysdig blog analysis of the Kinsing malware, which targets misconfigured cloud native environments such as exposed Docker engines. Kinsing acts as a loader: it downloads and runs a Monero crypto miner (kdevtmpfsi), disables security tools, kills rival miners, sets up cronjob persistence, reads SSH keys to move laterally, and contacts command and control servers. Detection advice uses Falco.
